raw_response:
Well, let me think this through. At my age, with these old bones, I don't go chasing new things. I've been growing cotton on this land since before my son was born, and I know what works here.

My 5 mu isn't much, but it's mine. With just me and the old lady at home — the kids are in the city now — I have to think about what we can actually manage. Cotton picking kills my back these days, but it's still the best cash crop for our western Quzhou soil, and the price last autumn was decent. So I'll put 4 mu in cotton, and keep 1 mu aside for mungbean. The mungbean is for us — my wife likes to make soup with it in summer — and whatever extra we sell at the market in Quzhou town brings a bit of pocket money. Mungbean doesn't ask much of you, and it's good for the soil before I rotate cotton back next year.

For cotton, I'll stick with the Bt hybrid seed I bought last year from the agricultural supply shop — 60-something yuan for a mu's worth. That seed handles the bollworm so I don't have to spray as much. I lay plastic mulch (地膜) before planting around 20 April, the way everyone here does — keeps the soil warm and holds the moisture. 

Fertilizer — I put down one bag of 15-15-15 compound before planting, about 40 kg per mu, that's my base. Then at flowering I topdress urea, maybe 15 kg per mu if the plants look pale. So all together that works out to about 13-14 kg N per mu. The extension fellow at the township station told me a few years back to do 18 kg, but honestly on my land 14 is enough — I've tried more and the bolls don't set any better, just waste my money. Phosphorus and potassium about 6 kg each per mu from the compound.

I'll irrigate twice — once right after planting if the spring is dry, and once at boll-setting in July. Pumping from my well isn't free, the electric meter runs the whole time, so I don't waste water. If the rains come I'll skip one.

Pesticide — I spray for aphids in late May, and watch for bollworm even with Bt seed. Maybe 3 sprays over the season. I'll use whatever the shop recommends, nothing fancy.

Labor is the hard part. My wife and I can handle planting and spraying, but picking cotton in September-October at my age? I'll need to pay my niece's husband and a couple of village women to help with the last two picks. That's maybe 400-500 yuan out the door, but I can't do it alone anymore.

For the mungbean on 1 mu — I plant late May after the ground warms up, use seed I saved from last year, hardly any fertilizer, no irrigation unless it's bone dry. It's an easy crop. Harvest in August before cotton gets busy.

I keep a little cash back for the bad times — you never know when the cotton price will drop or a hailstorm will hit. 50 years of farming teaches you that.
